 JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death caused in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 21.08.2023 at about 10.20 a.m, the deceased was proceeding along with Mr. Raghu as a pillion rider on Nandini Layout Ring Road,
towards Summanahalli Bridge on a motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-ED-5570.

When they reached near H.P.Petrol Bunk, Outer Ring Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru City, at that time the rider of the motorcycle / Mr. Raghu drove the motorcycle with high speed, rash and negligent manner without observing any traffic rules and regulations and lost the control over the motorcycle.
As a result of which the deceased and the rider of the motorcycle fell on the road along with motorcycle.

At that time, one driver of the Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-1026, who was coming on the same road and same direction came with a high speed, in rash and negligent manner,
endangering human life without following the traffic rules and passed over on the deceased and caused the accident.
Due to the terrific impact the pillion rider / deceased sustained grievous injuries to his head and other parts of the body and succumbed to the injuries and died on the spot.

It is alleged that after the accident the deceased was shifted to Victoria Hospital, wherein Postmortem was conducted and the corpse was handed over to the family members who conducted funeral and other ceremonies by spending substantial amount.
Further at the time of accident the deceased was working labourer and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and contributing the same for the maintenance of the family.
It is alleged that due to the sad demise of the deceased, the petitioners were undergoing deep mental shock and agony.
It is further urged that the accident happened because of rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle and driver of the Water Tanker.
Respondent No.1 being the owner of the Motorcycle and respondent No.2 being the owner of the Water Tanker are liable to pay the compensation.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1, the respondent No.1 did not appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he placed exparte.
4. Notice was duly served to respondent No.2.

Respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel by filing written statement rather objections to the main petition contending that the petition itself is Mithu Sahis vs Srinivas Raja .H on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187456586/

sentences.text: not maintainable either law or on facts.
The respondent No.2 admitted that he is the RC owner of the water tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-1026.
This respondent contended that accident in question did not occur on account of the rash and negligent driving of the vehicle, the accident occurred due to negligence of rider of the motorcycle.
Admittedly the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50- ED-5570 had consumed alcohol and was driving the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life.
The accident in question is occurred purely on the negligence of the rider of motorcycle and there is no negligent on the part of the driver of the water tanker.

Further the police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the motorcycle for the offences punishable u/s 279, 304A of IPC and Section 185, 3(1) r/w 181 of IMV Act and the police have filed charge sheet against the respondent No.2 u/s 146, 196 of IMV Act.
Hence there is no negligence on the part of this respondent.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation.
Further denied all the allegation made in the petition.
Hence prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioners prove that they are the legal heir and dependents of the deceased ?
2) Whether the petitioners prove

that the deceased succumbed to the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 21.08.2023 at about 10.20 a.m.,
near H.P. Petrol Bunk, outer ring road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, due to the composite negligence of the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-50-ED-5570 and the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-1026 ?
3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation as prayed ?

If so, at what rate and from whom ?
4) What order or award ?
6. The Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 16 were marked on behalf of the petitioners.
In order to prove the defence, the respondent No.2 did not choose lead evidence.
7. Heard counsel for the petitioners.
In spite of sufficient opportunity has been granted, respondent No.2 has not addressed his arguments.
Therefore arguments of respondent No.2 is taken as nil.

In spite of liberty has been given to the respondent No.2 to address his arguments or filing of written arguments before 2 days of date of pronouncement of judgment, he has neither addressed oral arguments nor filed written arguments.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative  Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.4 : As per final order Mithu Sahis vs Srinivas Raja .H on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187456586/
3  for the following :
 REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.2: The occurrence of the accident on the relevant date, time and place is not in dispute.

sentences.text: The only issue with which the parties are at loggerheads is with regard to the factum of negligence.

The evidence on record reveals that after the receipt of complaint, the jurisdictional police conducted thorough investigation and filed charge sheet against the driver of rider of Honda Dio S c o o t e r b e a r i n g R e g .

146, 196, 5(1) r/w 180 of IMV Act and further the charge sheet also filed against the owner of the motorcycle for the offences punishable u/s's 5(1), 180, 146, 196 of IMV Act and also filed charge sheet against owner of the water tanker u/s 146, 196 of IMV Act.
9.
The IO has issued notice u/s 133 of MV Act as per Ex.P.10, the owner of the Water Tanker has replied to the notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P.11.
Wherein the owner of the Water Tanker has admitted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Further he has admitted that the driver of his Water tanker name is Siddaraju and was having valid DL.
Further in his reply the insurance company details is mentioned as Nil.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of accident the water tanker is not having valid insurance.
Further the IO has also issued notice u/s 133 of MV Act as per Ex.P.12, the owner of the Dio Scooter bearing Reg.No.KA-50-D-5570 has replied to the notice u/s 133 of IMV Act as per Ex.P.13.
Wherein the owner of the Dio scooter has admitted the involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Further he has admitted that the rider of his scooter by name is Raghu.
Further in his reply Driving Licence number column, issuance of office details, issued date and also the insurance policy number and its insurance column details is mentioned as Nil.
Hence it is clear that as on the date of accident the rider of the Dio scooter is not having valid DL to ride the motorcycle and further the said vehicle is also not having valid insurance.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Inspite of due service of the notice of petition upon respondent No.1, he failed to appear before this Tribunal.
Hence he was placed exparte.
Further the respondent No.2 appeared and filed his written statement but he has not examined any witness before this Court.
Sufficient time is granted for cross examination of PW.1, but the respondent No.2 has not cross examined the PW.1.
Hence cross of PW.1 is taken as no cross.
Thus the evidence led by the petitioners has remained unchallenged.

Be that as it may the inference that can be drawn from the police documents and evidence of PW.1 is that the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-ED-5570 and driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-1026 were equally responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
Thereby the negligence attributed towards each of them is 50%.

With this observation Issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
10. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner No.1 filed affidavit in lieu of her chief-examination and deposed that she is the mother of deceased and petitioners No.2 and 3 are the younger brother of deceased.
PW.1 in her affidavit evidence she deposed that her husband was died and the petitioner No.3 is mentally challenged, her deceased son was taken responsibility of the entire family.

The documents i.e., Ex.P1 to 4 notarized copies of the Aadhaar cards of petitioners No.1 and 2 and deceased and Mithu Sahis vs Srinivas Raja .H on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187456586/
4 disability certificate of petitioner No.3 placed on record reflect the aforesaid relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.

sentences.text: Since the evidence led by PW.1 is satisfactory and also taking into consideration the fact that there are no rival claimants, hence, I hold that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased.
Accordingly, this Tribunal answers issue No.1 In the Affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.3: LOSS OF DEPENDENCY :
In the Aadhaar card (Ex.P.1) the date of birth of deceased is reflected as 03.02.2004.
This indicates that he was aged (19 years 6 months 18 days) 20 years at the time of accident.

Therefore the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group is '18'.
12.
In this case the petitioners have claimed the compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- on the death of deceased in the road traffic accident.
The petitioners contended that deceased was working as labour and earning of Rs.20,000/-p.m.
However neither the avocation and income of the deceased is substantiated by producing cogent materials nor any witness is examined in this regard.
In the absence of authentic proof of income of the deceased, this Tribunal has to consider his income notionally for calculating the compensation.
Admittedly the accident took place in the year 2023.
It is trite law that, when the petitioners have failed to prove the income, the income of the deceased has to be taken into consideration as notional income.
It is relevant to rely on a decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka rendered on Division Bench in the case of Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV) dated.05.07.2023.

entities.text: Ananda v/s Arjun and another in MFA.No.101144/2020 (MV)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has laid down the following principles in para No.8(b) are as here under :
"(b) The accident is of the year 2017.
The Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.7,000/- per month as against the claim of Rs.2,50,000/- per annum.
To substantiate the said claim, the injured claimant has not placed any material on record, it is for the Courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/-.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/- per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant"
As such this court is taking the notional income as prescribed by the Karnataka Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
Therefore in view of the above decision, the accident was occurred on 21.08.2023.
Therefore, Rs.16,000/- has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the deceased.

13. As per the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2017 ACJ 2700 (SC) (National Insurance Company Limited Vs Pranay Sethi and others), if the person died in the motor accident, the income with respect to the future prospect has to taken into consideration while awarding compensation.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Apex Court has provide the chart for age of the deceased and percentage for future prospects in between below the age of 40 years 40%, 40 years to 50 years 25% and 50 to 60 years 10%.

The deceased is not a permanent Employee and not a fixed salary person and he died at the age Mithu Sahis vs Srinivas Raja .H on 7 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187456586/
5 of 20 years.

sentences.text: Therefore, in this case, 40% income has to be taken into consideration for future prospects.

Further as stated above that, as on the date of accident, deceased aged about 20 years and as such, 40% is added to the income of the deceased, then it comes to Rs.22,400/- p.m. (Rs.16,000 + 6,400/- i.e. 40%).
14. Further as stated above that, deceased was a bachelor, as per the decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla verma V/s.
Delhi Transport Corporation

, the 50% of the income of the deceased shall be deducted towards his personal expenses as the deceased unmarried, thereby the 50% income of the deceased has to be deducted for his personal expenditure.

On such deduction,
the income of the deceased comes to Rs.11,200/- p.m. (Rs.22,400 X 50/100).
15. The income of the deceased is taken as Rs.11,200/- p.m. and the multiplier '18' is applied, then the loss of dependency comes to Rs.24,19,200/- (Rs.11,200 X 12 X 18)

Considering the above facts,
this Tribunal deems it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.24,19,200/- under the head of loss of dependency.

16. Further, as Law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, the compensation towards loss to estate, funeral expenses and consortium is to be awarded.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The petitioners contended that they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies etc., but no documents are produced.
Hence this Tribunal award Rs.18,150/- towards loss to estate and Rs.18,150/- towards funeral expenses as enhanced at the rate of 10% on every 3 years.

17. In this case, petitioner No.1 is the mother of the deceased and as per the decision reported in (2018) 12 SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others, the petitioners are entitled for filial consortium, as the filial consortium is the right of the parents to compensation in the case of an accidental death of a child.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Company Limited V/s Nanu Ram alias Chuhru Ram and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: An accident leading to the death of a child causes great shock and agony to the parents and family of the deceased.
The greatest agony for a parent is to lose of their child during their lifetime.
Children are valued for their love, affection, companionship and their oral in the family unit.

Therefore,
petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.40,000/- under the head of Filial consortium.

18. The calculation table stands as follows :
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1. Towards loss of dependency Rs.24,19,200/-
2. Towards loss to estate Rs. 18,150/-
3.Towards transportation of dead Rs. 18,150/-

19.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
20. The respondent No.1 is stated to be the owner of the Motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-ED-5570 and respondent No.2 is stated to be the owner of the Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-1026.
They have not produced any document to show that their respective vehicles had insurance coverage at the time of accident.
Further the rider of the motorcycle was also not possessing valid DL to ride the motorcycle on the date of accident.
It is well settled that a person driving a vehicle is presumed to have authority to do the same unless the contrary is proved.

In the absence of any contrary evidence in this regard and also considering the fact that the claimant has established that the accident was caused by the rider of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-ED-5570 and driver of the Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-1026.
Admittedly it is a case of composite negligence where the deceased has sustained injuries and died due to the accident and has been caused by a combined wrongful act of joint tortfeasor.

Under such circumstances, each wrong doer i.e., the respondents No.1 & 2 herein are jointly & severally liable and accordingly directed to pay the aforesaid award amount to the claimants together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.

However the respondents No.1 & 2 being the owners of motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-50-ED-5570 and Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-53-AA-1026 are primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest in the ratio of 50 : 50, within one month from the date of this order.
Accordingly Issue No.3 is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.
21. ISSUE NO.4 :

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle's Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.24,95,500/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.
The respondents No.1 & 2 are liable to pay and directed to deposit the aforesaid amount together with interest in the ratio of 50 : 50, within a period of one month from the date of award.

On deposit of the award amount together with interest, the claimants are entitled for the compensation amount by way of apportionment as follows :
 Petitioner No.1 - 50%
 Petitioner No.2 - 30%
 Petitioner No.3 - 20%

However the said petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.

The share amount apportioned in the name of minor petitioners No.2 & 3 is ordered to be deposited in their names vide Fixed Deposit till they attain the age of majority,
at any Nationalized/Scheduled Bank as per the choice of the next friend/Natural guardian of the said minor petitioners.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
